Mobile EEG during walking
I record EEG during walking and combine it with motion capture, EMG and wearable sensors to study cortical contributions to gait, for example gait-related beta oscillations and corticomuscular coherence, and their changes in Parkinson’s disease.

title: StepuP: Steps against the burden of Parkinson’s disease
text:
Aims
Speed-dependent treadmill training (SDTT) improves gait in Parkinson’s disease, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. StepuP tests two hypotheses: that training improves stability-related foot placement, i.e. the step-to-step adjustment of foot placement to the state of the body’s centre of mass, and that it improves cortical sensorimotor integration, measured as gait-related EEG beta power and EEG–EMG (corticomuscular) coherence. Secondary aims are to compare standard SDTT with an enriched protocol (SDTT+, with virtual reality or mechanical perturbations) and to assess transfer to walking in daily life.

title: StepuP: Steps against the burden of Parkinson’s disease
text:
Design
StepuP consists of three harmonised, parallel randomised controlled trials with a shared core protocol at clinical sites in Kiel, Bologna, Tel Aviv and Sydney. Each trial includes 42 people with Parkinson’s disease (126 in total). A reference group of 21 healthy older adults is measured in Amsterdam. Participants are randomised to standard speed-dependent treadmill training (SDTT) or to SDTT+, and complete twelve 30-minute training sessions. Depending on the site, SDTT+ adds virtual-reality obstacles, mechanical belt perturbations, or both.
Assessments take place at baseline, after training and at a 12-week follow-up and comprise:

Synchronised 64-channel EEG, EMG and 3D motion capture during treadmill walking at comfortable and fixed speeds, plus resting-state EEG
Clinical testing, e.g. MDS-UPDRS III, Mini-BESTest, MoCA, Trail Making Test, Timed Up and Go, falls self-efficacy and quality of life
One week of daily-life monitoring with a lower-back inertial sensor (digital mobility outcomes)

The primary clinical endpoint is comfortable overground walking speed. Mechanistic outcomes include stride length and stride time, the explained variance and error of a foot-placement model, EEG beta power and corticomuscular coherence. They are analysed with linear mixed-effects models.

title: StepuP: Steps against the burden of Parkinson’s disease
text:
Data acquisition and standardisation
The sites use different EEG, EMG and motion-capture systems. All data streams are synchronised with the Lab Streaming Layer and converted into a common multi-site dataset in the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), with eeg, emg and motion data per participant and session, following Motion-BIDS for the motion data.

title: StepuP: Steps against the burden of Parkinson’s disease
text:
My role
Together with Walter Maetzler, I lead the Kiel site (University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein and Kiel University). Across the consortium, I am responsible for the multimodal recording and data-standardisation pipeline:

LSL synchronisation setup for the EEG, EMG and motion-capture systems
EEG data-quality checks
BIDS converter for the recordings and REDCap clinical data of all sites
EEG and BIDS training sessions at consortium meetings

I am shared first author of the study protocol with Moira van Leeuwen.

title: EEGManySteps
text:
Aims
EEGManySteps is a community initiative in mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI). Instead of replicating a single experiment, it collects and harmonises gait EEG recorded with different setups, including existing datasets and new recordings, to identify which acquisition and analysis factors most affect the consistency of gait-related EEG results.
The initiative addresses four research questions:

step-specific time-frequency patterns,
gait-related artefacts across EEG systems,
the influence of preprocessing on EEG results during walking, and
gait-related modulation of secondary-task correlates such as the P3.

title: EEGManySteps
text:
Data harmonisation
Contributed datasets are converted to EEG-BIDS and Motion-BIDS and annotated with additional metadata (indoor or outdoor, treadmill or overground, footwear, secondary task, speed protocol, synchronisation method). Sensor locations follow the UNISEP vocabulary, and gait events are standardised. For new recordings, a harmonised auditory oddball paradigm is provided for standing and walking conditions.

title: IGOR: Interest Group on Open and Reproducible Research
text:
About IGOR
IGOR is a forum for members of the DGPs section Biological Psychology and Neuropsychology to exchange approaches for open and reproducible research. Its activities include community projects, training for early-career researchers and the annual IGOR Prize for Open and Reproducible Science. The founding document (in German) is available here.

title: IGOR: Interest Group on Open and Reproducible Research
text:
BIDS Consultation Hour
Since 2024 I have organised the IGOR BIDS Consultation Hour, an online forum in which researchers receive advice on converting their datasets to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS). I cover EEG and motion data; a colleague covers MRI. The website also collects BIDS training materials.

title: IGOR: Interest Group on Open and Reproducible Research
text:
EEG/ERP preprocessing umbrella review
With Yu-Fang Yang, Mario Reutter-Dieker and Johannes Rodrigues, I co-lead an umbrella review of EEG/ERP preprocessing practices. It synthesises how preprocessing pipelines and parameters are reported and justified in the literature, with the aim of shared extraction standards. The review is preregistered on OSF.

title: META-REP: Replicability of mobile EEG
text:
The programme
META-REP (A Meta-scientific Programme to Analyse and Optimise Replicability in the Behavioural, Social, and Cognitive Sciences) is a DFG Priority Programme (SPP 2317) on the replicability of findings and on methods to improve it. In Oldenburg, the METEOR project addresses the many defensible analysis decisions between a raw neural recording and a published result. My work within META-REP concerns these decisions in mobile EEG.

title: META-REP: Replicability of mobile EEG
text:
Background
Mobile EEG allows recordings during walking and other everyday movements. Compared with stationary EEG, it involves additional methodological decisions: hardware and cable management, synchronisation with motion sensors, detection of gait events, and the removal of movement artefacts, including the order and parameters of preprocessing steps.
In a review of studies combining mobile EEG with gait measurements (Vinod et al., 2026), we found large differences in the selection, order and combination of preprocessing steps, in particular in the tools and reporting of artefact rejection. Many pipelines were not described in enough detail to be reproduced. We concluded that standardised reporting, rather than a single mandatory pipeline, is needed to make studies comparable and reproducible. An earlier review of P3 studies during walking reached a similar conclusion (Jacobsen et al., 2025).

title: META-REP: Replicability of mobile EEG
section: A reporting standard for mobile EEG
text:
A reporting standard for mobile EEG
A reporting standard for mobile EEG studies is in preparation. It defines a minimum set of information to report, starting from the items most often missing in the review:


Recording context Setting and task, such as indoor or outdoor, treadmill or overground walking, and the equipment used.
Preprocessing steps Every step with its order and tools, in particular how movement artefacts are rejected.
Software parameters The settings of each tool, so that a pipeline can be re-run.
Open code and workflows Analysis code and workflows shared openly, ideally with data in community standards such as EEG-BIDS and Motion-BIDS.

title: Software
text:
KielMAT

The Kiel Motion Analysis Toolbox (KielMAT, formerly NGMT) is a Python toolbox for gait and balance analysis in neurological cohorts. It implements validated algorithms for wearable and motion-capture data and uses a data model based on Motion-BIDS.
Role: co-developer and co-maintainer
Documentation · PyPI · GitHub · JOSS paper
